claim_results.reason: The revised sign decision is algebraically sound within the declared domain: u0=0 and u1=1 give r2=A2/c0; while preceding steps are positive, dividing the recurrence by u_(m-1) gives r_m=(A_m-B_m/r_(m-1))/c0. Fraction arithmetic computes this ratio exactly, and floating logarithms never feed back into it. Fresh independent replays rejected both supplied counterexamples at m=4, whose exact final values are respectively 0 and -1/18014398509481984. An additional 105 constructed cases with nonunit normalizations and stopping indices through 64 correctly accepted 35 positive endpoints and rejected 70 zero or negative endpoints, including magnitudes 10^-1000. Conversion checks confirmed preservation of represented binary floats and exact decimal/rational inputs. The nextafter case computes the approximate logarithm of the exactly positive value 2^-53; an input already rounded to 1 correctly produces rejection of the resulting zero step. Empty prefixes, invalid coefficients, first-failure termination and extreme ratios were checked. Ratio denominators demonstrably grow: for A=3, B=2, c0=1, r_m=(2^m-1)/(2^(m-1)-1), consistent with the documented performance tradeoff.

All five frozen scripts exited successfully. Unmodified reviewer-owned copies of both harnesses passed all 17 behavior tests and all five minimal regressions with AUDIT_SOURCE_ROOT pointing to the frozen inputs. All ten injected failures raised AssertionError and exited nonzero, including five runs under -O. All 11 snapshot hashes and all seven source hashes recorded in RESULT.json matched; packet and snapshot hashes remained unchanged afterward. Checked normalization, large-rational growth diagnostics, initial values, quiet imports, preserved mpmath precision, log(k), finite sums and sparse indices. Independently expanding (c-D^2)(x^(2m)-alpha*x^(2m-2)) yields the implemented coefficients and boundary derivative -(2m-2)*delta. Under c0>0, B>=0 and eps>=0, monotonicity gives u_m>=(1+eps_m)u_(m-1), establishing the product lower bound; equality is restricted to the stated B=0 examples. The Gamma denominator is Gamma(2+C). The stated series thresholds follow analytically from terms proportional to m^(2C-2beta), or m^(-2beta)*(log m)^(2C); the stated equality cases diverge. Sparse indices are exactly 2^(2^j), j>=1, and consecutive jumps K and K^2 justify the stated last-jump bound. Finite numerical outputs are appropriately distinguished from these analytic statements.

limitations: Fresh execution used Python 3.14.4 and mpmath 1.3.0. Other runtime versions were not tested. Harness output was confined to a reviewer-owned temporary directory.
Logarithms remain floating approximations. These checks establish neither uniform error bounds nor interval certification, and cannot recover information lost before coefficient conversion.
Exact rational arithmetic can incur growing time and memory costs. No general large-N resource bound was established.
Historical execution provenance and author-reported timings were not independently reconstructed; current frozen implementations were freshly executed.
Approval is restricted to the two requested software-review claims and supplied snapshots. It does not establish project-wide mathematical completeness or complete formalization.
